en: Let us leave them thus;
The great army the giant Döödür reached,
Let us begin news of it.
Fleeing, great Döödür
To the tent with golden pillars,
That Döödür went,
To the warriors Döngö and Zholoy.
Lamps were lit in the tent.
When they saw warrior Döödür,
The many lords crowded round like a cauldron.
Their Torguts gathered in full;
Bells were rung hard.
The army lost its senses.
Now the many seething lords,
Of the Chinese with rank buttons on their caps,
The shaven-headed ones gathered.
Of the red-tufted Chinese,
The mighty ones gathered.
The warriors who cultivated wisdom,
To that Döödür's presence
Had come that day,
The warriors Döngö and Zholoy.
All came and stood;
When all had arrived,
They looked at warrior Döödür:
He was engulfed in dust,
Covered in a red bucketful of blood.
His two flailing arms
Could not rise, hanging paralyzed.
His dear head as big as a pail
Was covered in dark red blood.
“I was struck from the side;
To the fucking Burut
I lost my goods on forty camels.
He dug my pit deep.
At the hands of the fucking Burut,
I saw many wonders.
I let him work many wonders;
About two hundred wrestlers
I let his lone Manas slaughter.
Do not ask about Manas:
He is a child of twelve.
When he reaches nineteen,
Upon Beijing ruled by the kakan,
He is a hero who will wreak slaughter.
His right shoulder is broad.
The bloodthirsty Burut Manas,
The eighteen thousand worlds,
He is one who will lay them waste.
Do not ask about Manas:
Thick-armed, stone-hearted,
I have seen none like him in an age.
An elephant-limbed, dauntless hero,
He is the bloodthirsty Burut himself.
Beyond Manas himself,
Those are his very watching black eyes.
Life departs at his rumbling voice.
If you live, you will see:
The bloodthirsty Burut Manas,
Life departs at his wrath.
He is gray-maned, he is a lion,
Born plain for all to see.
If he lives, upon Beijing
He will bring uproar.
Ruling the people, holding a nation,
He has the bearing of a commander.
Blood flows wherever he charges;
He has the bearing of a wrestler.
He has a coat no bullet can pierce;
He has a horse no bullet can catch.
His brow is high, his venom strong.
When Manas charges and attacks,
Abandon hope of your dear life.
His armed companions number eighty-four,
That fucking Burut,
Wherever he sweeps is red fire.
He wears an unsheathed sword,
Carries a spear of red copper.
His face is like wheat rubbed with oil,
His eyes like twilight mist.
Drinking, he cannot get his fill of blood;
He spares none who face him.
His warrior spirit shows.
He will drive white deer as cattle;
If you live, you will see,
He will bring the world to submission.
Can any mortal face him?
The warrior Burut Manas,
Can anyone who meets him remain alive?
Among mortals I have seen none like him.
At one glance, he is one man;
That fucking Burut,
At another glance, a thousand men.
I looked at his front:
He has the terror of six thousand warriors.
I looked at his back:
He has the form of a lion.
He is a renowned and mighty support,
A warrior unlike other mortals.
A jekene belt girds his waist.
If seven milek of foes advance,
If frenzy seizes him and he attacks,
He has the form of a devouring monster.
He is a fierce gray-maned lion,
From the fucking Burut,
A warrior born unique.
I, who spare none I grapple with,
On the meat of a single pig,
Who cannot eat my fill in one sitting,
Whose wrestling strength is exceptional,
I picked a quarrel with Manas.
He unleashed fierce wrath.
My wrestlers numbered two hundred;
Their heads, one by one, he simply
Snapped off like rhubarb stalks.
My black-bladed battle-axe,
I seized and swung it.
Charging in at Manas,
I struck exactly ninety blows.
He hummed, unconcerned.
The axe blows he took from me,
He valued less than his trouser cuff.
When I used my strength, that Manas
Did not count me even as a fly.
What you drink will not pass your throat.
When Manas struck,
Our heads were torn to pieces.
I lost my means and was trapped;
The gray rhinoceros beneath me,
By its swiftness I fled and escaped.
“I shall bind Manas,” I said;
I grew careless of my own life.
Between death and life,
Here I lie wounded.
Saying I would impose my rule,
I scattered my own wealth.
I was struck on my vulnerable side.
About two hundred wrestlers
I lost to your Kyrgyz.
At one blow I was stopped.
If he strikes twice, what will happen?
Burning and blazing, I became an ember.
Let not one go, let a thousand go.
Let not a few go, let many go.
Let not your weak go, let your best go.
I have spoken; go heeding my words.
Manas is no easy foe.
Go with your ears alert to uproar.
Choose your heroes; let your warriors go.
Leave the solitary one; let your multitude go.
Let your weak remain; let your warriors go.
When the black gun cracks,
Let those go who will not flee.
When the short gun booms,
Let warriors go who will not flinch.
If one grapples with Manas,
No person's strength can equal him.
If one struggles with the bloodthirsty one,
Even a lion's teeth cannot pierce him.
No mortal can face him.
That wretched Burut is a warrior;
None who face him can remain alive.
Good heavens, his eyes are like grave pits!
If he sees you all,
He might swallow you with your horses.
If your bloodthirsty one grows angry,
He might seize you all
And simply mow you down like grass.
He does not draw back from his doom,
He does not turn back from death.
May that Burut's measure be damned!
That Manas was born
Of the people called Burut.
He is the very black eye of terror.
That Burut is not Manas,
He is simply uproar itself.
If this Manas reaches maturity,
He will break rock and make a road.
The seething kakan's realm,
Great Beijing, he will attack.
He will not let us turn the plow.
May I lose my portion if I lie:
He will not let us stay in this Beijing.
Smashing the stone fortress,
He is a hero who will raze it all.
Born among forty households,
We failed to see Manas;
Our eyes were clouded at that time.
If that Manas grows,
Beijing ruled by the kakan,
He is a lion who will make it wail.
To the people of this Beijing,
He is a hero who will bring havoc.
I have seen the Burut Manas,
These people called Burut.
Islam is their faith in their hearts;
They are our enemies at their root.
No mortal can come against him.
If we drive all Beijing's people forth,
They cannot match Manas's strength.
No person can make him bow.
This ill-omened Burut,
None who meet him can remain alive.
The very crown of my head aches;
Every measured part of me aches.
I have no strength to move.
If I return to the Burut,
To those people called Burut,
I have no means to face them.
My vigor is spent, my strength gone.
From all my whole body,
Dark blood poured in throbbing pain.
Since I became the giant Döödür,
Since I won the name Döödür,
When I fought Madangshang,
Destroyed his city with its court,
Plundered and loaded his gold,
And returned having made him submit,
I was never like this then.”
As Döödür stood speaking thus,
Döngö came forth with force;
Zholoy came forth speaking:
“Of the fucking Burut,
Of the people called Burut,
You have grown afraid!
Warrior Zholoy, warrior Döngö,
We have raided the Burut people.
These are the hands that seized them;
This is the mouth that challenged them.
We have seen the Burut;
We plundered their goods,
Wrought havoc upon them thus.
Driving one to Eren,
The fucking Burut,
We cast many into the depths.
This is the road we have surveyed;
These are the hands that seized them!
He is a child of twelve;
We shall bind their Manas.
If rich Jakyp falls into our hands,
We shall slaughter him as a sacrifice.
We shall kill their honored men;
The fucking Burut,
We shall put them in black mourning headwraps.”
Saying so, warrior Zholoy
Hurried the great army.
Achbuudan beneath him,
He made it stride over rises and hollows.
Draping himself in blue armor,
If you saw warrior Zholoy,
He raged like a blue tiger.
Bulging in his short coat,
The sight unsettled the heart.
Do not ask about Zholoy:
He loomed like a towering mountain.
On one side, warrior Döngö,
